critique: Assertion 1 is the weak spot: it says 'same stylesheet' but the with_skill surface vendors the AUTHORITY token sheet, not the app's global.css, and passes token discipline while still making a zero pixel diff impossible — the assertion should name the file (app/src/styles/global.css, or a byte-identical copy) and require a checkable import line, otherwise a nearly-equivalent token sheet reads as a pass. Assertion 2 is satisfied here but cannot distinguish a meaningful live capture from an empty shell: the run honestly shot :4174 and got a page with no Git section at all, so the headline pixelDiff measures absent content, not drift. A better assertion would require the shot to contain the state under test (e.g. a `.git` section present) or an explicit 'state not reachable' verdict with the gate marked inconclusive rather than FAIL. Assertion 5 is checkable only because the skill writes state.json/prompts/attempts — it is unverifiable for a no-skill run. No assertion checks the accuracy of the per-element pixel table (e.g. divider x=333/922, Solution row 39px), which is the user's actual ask ('tell me exactly where the app differs, in pixels'); spot-checks against git-panel-app.png agree, but a fabricated table would pass every current assertion.

suggestions.assertion: The surface imports or vendors the same stylesheet the implementation uses, so a zero pixel diff is achievable
suggestions.reason: Passes-by-proximity risk: a vendored authority token sheet one commit ahead of the app's copy is 'almost' the same stylesheet. Require an import of global.css (or a byte-identical copy) verifiable by grep/diff.

suggestions.assertion: Shot the live URL with the same viewport as the surface and produced translate/diff/<state>-app/report.json with pixelDiff
suggestions.reason: The live capture was a real shot of an empty shell; the assertion should require the target state be present in the shot or the gate be reported as inconclusive, not just that a report.json exists.
No assertion checks that the reported per-element pixel deltas are correct against the app screenshot — the core user request.

eval_feedback.overall: Discriminating on the two-numbers point (assertion 3) and on the report artifact (2); weak on stylesheet identity (1) and silent on measurement accuracy.
